### Data
Load and preprocess the collected data

```{r}
DATA_DIR <- "../data/"

wide_df <- read.csv(file.path(DATA_DIR, "participant_data.csv"), check.names = TRUE)
long_df <- read.csv(file.path(DATA_DIR, "participant_data_long.csv"), check.names = TRUE)
eod_df <- read.csv(file.path(DATA_DIR, "participant_data_eod.csv"), check.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Collapse the sparse demographic levels that would otherwise be singleton cells.
collapse_levels <- function(x, other, other_label = "Other") {
  x <- as.character(x)
  factor(ifelse(x %in% other, other_label, x))
}

wide_df <- wide_df %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_treatment = ifelse(baseline_treatment == "True", 1, 0),
    treatment = as_treatment(baseline_treatment),
    wave      = factor(wave),
    baseline_Gender = collapse_levels(baseline_Gender, c("2", "4")),
    baseline_Race   = collapse_levels(baseline_Race,   c("3", "4", "5", "6", "7")),
    Relationship = factor(
      case_when(
        baseline_Relationship == 0                ~ "Single",
        baseline_Relationship %in% c(1, 2, 3)     ~ "In Relationship",
        baseline_Relationship %in% c(4, 5, 6, 7)  ~ "Other",
        TRUE                                      ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("Single", "In Relationship", "Other")
    )
  )
```



### Helper Functions
Add helper function to rescale to baseline standard deviation
```{r}
dvs <- unique(c(
  "loneliness", 
  "wb", 
  "esi", 
  "BPNSFS_Autonomy",   
  "BPNSFS_Competence",
  "BPNSFS_Relatedness", 
  "lubben", "social_satisfaction", "ppl_met_inperson",
  "problematic_use", "belief", 
  "is_weekend", "date_since_start"
))

# Every wave from randomization through the end of the deactivation window.
# The post-resumption wave lives in "Post Analyses.qmd", not here.
timepoints    <- c("baseline", "diary1", "midline", "diary2", "endline")
baseline_covs <- c("Age", "Gender", "EdLevel", "Income", "Race")
other_covs    <- c("Tenure", "Usage", "Social", "Productivity", "Relationship", "Novelty", "Entertainment", "isProductivityMain", "isSocialMain")

sd_table <- function(stats) {
  data.frame(
    outcome       = names(stats),
    baseline_mean = vapply(stats, `[[`, numeric(1), "mean"),
    baseline_sd   = vapply(stats, `[[`, numeric(1), "sd"),
    n_baseline    = vapply(stats, `[[`, numeric(1), "n"),
    row.names     = NULL
  )
}

# Rescale `vars` in `data` using `stats`, the moments of the pre-deactivation rows.
rescale_to_baseline <- function(data, vars, stats) {
  for (v in vars) {
    s <- stats[[v]]["sd"]
    if (is.na(s) || s == 0) next        # no usable baseline -> leave in raw units
    data[[v]] <- as.vector((data[[v]] - stats[[v]]["mean"]) / s)
  }
  data
}

z_vars <- setdiff(dvs, c("date_since_start", "is_weekend"))

long_stats <- lapply(z_vars, function(v) baseline_moments(long[[v]][long$time == "baseline"]))
names(long_stats) <- z_vars

long_z <- rescale_to_baseline(long, z_vars, long_stats)

# Reference table: what "1 SD" means for each outcome.
sd_table(long_stats)
```
```{r}
eod_z_vars <- c("esi", "happy", "depressed", "anxious",
                "time_worked", "time_socializing", "log_num_interactions")

eod_stats <- lapply(eod_z_vars, function(v) {
  baseline_moments(eod_z[[v]][eod_z$days_since_start == 0])
})
names(eod_stats) <- eod_z_vars

eod_z <- rescale_to_baseline(eod_z, eod_z_vars, eod_stats)
```

Helper functions for fitting statistical models

```{r}
person_covs <- c("wave", "baseline_Age", "baseline_Gender", "baseline_Race",
                 "baseline_EdLevel", "baseline_Income", "Relationship",
                 "Tenure", "Usage", "Social", "Productivity")

controls        <- paste(c(person_covs, "is_weekend"), collapse = " + ")

re_pid  <- "(1 | pid)"
re_long <- "(1 + days_since_start | pid)"
# Random slopes make the likelihood harder to optimize; bobyqa with a raised
# iteration cap converges where the default nloptwrap reports false positives.
lmer_ctrl <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

fit_primary <- function(dv, data = long_z) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("treatment * isDeactivation", controls, re_pid), response = dv),
       data = data, control = lmer_ctrl)
}

fit_eod_primary <- function(dv, data = eod_z) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("treatment * isDeactivation", controls, re_pid), response = dv),
       data = data, control = lmer_ctrl)
}

fit_eod_days <- function(dv, data = eod_z) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("treatment * days_since_start", controls, re_long), response = dv),
       data = data, control = lmer_ctrl)
}
```

## Results
### Primary Outcomes
These models correspond to outcomes reported in Sec. 2.1 in the main body of the paper.
#### ESI
```{r}
summary(fit_primary("esi"))
```
#### Psychological Well-Being
```{r}

summary(fit_primary("wb"))
```

### Moderators
The analyses correspond to the results reported in Sec. 2.3.
```{r}
fit_moderator <- function(dv, moderator, data = long_z) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(
      c(paste0("treatment * isDeactivation * ", moderator),
        controls, re_pid),
      response = dv
    ),
    data = data,
    control = lmer_ctrl
  )
}
```

```{r}
summary(fit_moderator("loneliness", "Usage"))
```

```{r}
summary(fit_moderator("loneliness", "Tenure"))
```
